findings.detail: after_suite and baseline_suite both name scratch/gate_imports2.log, whose own header is '=== head 0390ababc23e60eb0dcf6e84d9dcc8ab290e53ad', and the manifest's gate paragraph states 'the commits after it are docs only, so both arms describe this head' - but the head is 74491e00e, 'test(prescribed_plasma): wrap the two lines that ran past the column limit', a test-file change that also postdates the manifest's mtime. That commit's message claims 'The gate job is rerun at this revision'; the rerun exists as scratch/gate_imports3.log (job 1292464, header '=== head 74491e00ef9d6fa35b5cc0afbc0efcf64431bcdd') and its head arm collected nothing: nine consecutive 'ERROR: file or directory not found' with EXIT_FILE=<file>=4 for every gate file, because gate_final.sh runs pytest on relative paths while the job's working directory was not the worktree, and its header prints nova.__file__ = /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/nova/__init__.py rather than the worktree's. Only the base arm ran there. The manifest's artifact list also omits 74491e00e from the commits carrying the closure. The repair is cheap (rerun the gate at 74491e00e with the worktree as the job's working directory, or re-point the rows at the 0390ababc gate and record 74491e00e as whitespace-only), but as stored the reviewed head has no gate of its own.
findings.summary: the suite rows name revision 0390ababc while the reviewed head is 74491e00e, and the reviewed head's own gate rerun ran no head arm at all, so the reviewed revision carries no valid gate measurement.

findings.detail: nova/circuit/linkage.py:87 computes 0.5*abs(dot(r, roll(z,-1)) - dot(z, roll(r,-1))), the same expression as the public nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py:300 polygon_area(r, z) (listed in that module's __all__ at wall_mask.py:62) and as nova/imas/diiid_machine_ids.py:194 _shoelace_area. It duplicates rather than calls or extends either owner; the only differences are the input shape ((N,2) vertices against two arrays) and the dropped size<3 guard.
findings.summary: polygon_area re-implements the absolute shoelace area the repository already owns, without extending the owner.

findings.detail: nova/circuit/linkage.py:96 returns interior points and area weights summing to one for one polygon section; nova/imas/mast_passive_inductance.py:175 section_quadrature already does that job, by a bounding-box grid with a containment filter. The node consolidated the (r, z, weight, owner) concatenation into the existing section_grid owner at nova/circuit/linkage.py:143, which is the right move, and records the residual duplication as a follow-on in the fragment; but the quadrature rule itself is a second implementation of an owned capability, so the improvement belongs at the owner.
findings.summary: polygon_quadrature duplicates the interior-section quadrature capability owned by section_quadrature rather than extending it.

findings.detail: The fan at nova/circuit/linkage.py:110-122 fans triangles (apex=corners[0], corners[i], corners[i+1]) and takes each sub-triangle's centroid as a quadrature point, and every consumer weights plasma flux at those points by sub-triangle area. For a convex section that is exact; for a concave one the fan's triangles lie only partly inside the polygon, so points and their weights fall outside it, while the docstring asserts every point 'lies inside the section by construction ... whatever its shape, thickness or orientation'. The rule it replaced filtered its grid with shapely contains_xy before normalising, so this is a latent weakening of the guard the repair removed. The machine's shaped sections in use are thin convex quads and tests/test_prescribed_plasma.py:448 asserts containment on the tested sliver, so no current caller reaches the concave case; a section that is not star-shaped from its first corner would be sampled outside itself.
findings.summary: the triangle fan covers the polygon only if it is star-shaped from its first corner, and the containment filter the replaced rule applied was dropped.

findings.detail: tests/test_unseen_source_full_plant.py:350-403 is the only coverage of the reconstruction-style presentation, and every assertion inside it (the plasma_times equality at :390 and the two assert_allclose calls at :391-396) sits inside an arm that is expected to fail. A regression there cannot redden the suite; only an unexpected pass can. That is honest about the open measurement, and the live plan defers check 3 to dd-cocos-ingest section 3, but the durability of this path rests on no assertion.
findings.summary: the reconstruction arm is xfail(strict=True), so nothing in it can fail the suite and the reconstruction path has no regression guard.

findings.detail: tests/test_unseen_source_full_plant.py:363 reads 'the relative tolerance section-5 predeclared', citing a plan section from source. The naming rules ban plan and section references in docstrings and comments, because the source must read without the plan; the same sentence reads cleanly as 'the predeclared relative tolerance'.
findings.summary: a plan-section reference in a docstring leaks a plan label into source.

findings.detail: ruff check over the six changed Python files returns exactly one finding, tests/test_unseen_source_full_plant.py:401 E501 (100 > 88), in the f-string printing the reconstruction arm's measured extremes. The head commit 74491e00e exists to wrap two over-long lines in tests/test_prescribed_plasma.py and left this third one in place, so the file still fails a lint run that names it.
findings.summary: a 100-column line survives in the new test file, the one file the head's own column-wrap commit did not reach.
